subtopics.title: Why One Equation Has Infinitely Many Answers

questions.question: For sin x = 0,8 the calculator gives 53,13°. The second solution in the first turn is:
A trigonometric equation has infinitely many solutions because:
options: the functions repeat with every full period, in both directions

questions.question: The reference angle is defined as:
options: the acute angle whose ratio matches the size of the value, sign ignored

questions.question: The one-sentence summary of the method is:
options: the calculator answers once; the quadrants double it; the period multiplies it forever
the quadrants answer once; the calculator doubles it
the period answers once; the calculator multiplies it
one answer is always enough if it is exact

questions.question: For 5 sin x + 2 = 0, the first-turn solutions are:

options: typing the negative value into the calculator

subtopics.title: Tangent, and Equations That Need Tidying First

questions.question: Tangent's period is:
options: 180°, because a half-turn flips both y and x, leaving the fraction unchanged
360°, the same as sine and cosine

questions.question: The general solution of tan x = √3 is:

options: division by a variable expression is always allowed
if cos x were zero, sin x would be ±1 and the equation would claim ±√3 = 0 — impossible

options: substitute small integer values of k and keep only results inside the interval

options: solve it with the quadrant rules

questions.question: In the taxi picture, the letter k in a general solution is:
options: a lap counter — how many full loops forward or backward
the number of taxis on the route

options: tangent is negative in two quadrants

options: a seat passes the same height once going up and once coming down
